title: One Programme to a Legal Entity — Corporate Travel Programmes
content:
## The rule of holding

One contracting company holds exactly one corporate travel programme, and a second programme is never opened for the same legal entity. The ceiling on the Corporate Travel Programmes is accordingly 1 programme for each contracting company.

A group of companies with separate legal entities holds one programme per entity, and the entities are billed separately even where one address administers them all.

Where a company has somehow acquired two programmes, the older is kept, the seats and the balance of the younger are merged into it, and the younger is closed.

A traveller is not a programme: travellers occupy seats on a programme and hold their own personal club membership entirely separately.

## The same rule stated as a register entry

| What is presented | What the register holds |
| --- | --- |
| One legal entity | One corporate travel programme, and no second one opened for it |
| A group of several legal entities | One programme for each entity, each entity billed separately |
| One administering address covering several entities | Still one programme per entity, still billed separately |
| Two programmes standing against one company | The older kept, the seats and the balance of the younger merged into it, the younger closed |
| A named traveller | Not a programme: a seat on a programme, and a personal club membership held entirely separately |

## Applied to three arrangements

A holding company and its two operating subsidiaries are three separate legal entities. On this rule they hold three corporate travel programmes between them, one for each entity, and each entity is billed on its own account even though one office administers all three.

A company that already holds a corporate travel programme presents a request for a second one for the same legal entity. No second programme is opened for that entity.

A company whose records show two programmes against the same legal entity keeps the older of the two. The seats and the balance of the younger are merged into the older, and the younger is closed; nothing is carried the other way.
